wylie: dper na rta lta bu gcig la yang rgya gar rgya nag bod sog po sogs kyis rang rang gi yul skad sna tshogs kyi ming gis brjod pa bzhin dang, sher phyin byams pas zhus pa las gzugs sogs kyi chos thams cad la yang ming glo bur du btags par gsungs pas ming 'jug pa ni brda'i dbang yin gyi, dngos po'i dbang gis min no
english: We see for example the single object of a horse referred to in a variety of words from different languages—languages like Sanskrit or Chinese, or Tibetan or Mongolian. And the text on the perfection of wisdom requested by Maitreya states as well that the words which apply to every single object there is, from physical form on up, are applied artificially.[152] As such, the way that names apply to their objects is something that occurs only in words, and not through some natural connection.
